subject: anthropology
topicTitle: Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, Neolithic and Megalithic Cultures of India

ncertReference.chapter: Unit II: Prehistoric Cultures of India

thirtySecondSummary: Archaeological Anthropology reconstructs past human cultures through the systematic study of material remains, lithic technology, and palaeo-environmental contexts across the Pleistocene and Holocene epochs.

The Lower Palaeolithic in India is characterized by two distinct tool traditions: the Sohan Pebble Tool Tradition (chopper-chopping tools, Punjab) and the Acheulian Handaxe-Cleaver Tradition (Madrasian culture, Attirampakkam, Bhimbetka, Hunsgi).

The Middle Palaeolithic (Nevasan culture, H.D. Sankalia) transformed toolkits into smaller flake tools (scrapers, borers, points) struck from prepared cores; the Upper Palaeolithic witnessed parallel-sided blade and burin industries, bone tools, and ostrich eggshell beads (Patne, Kurnool caves).

The Mesolithic marks an environmental transition to the Holocene, characterized by geometric Microliths (trapezes, triangles, crescents), semi-sedentary hunting-foraging camps (Bagor, Langhnaj, Sarai Nahar Rai), and magnificent prehistoric rock art (Bhimbetka).

The Neolithic Revolution introduced food production (Mehrgarh early wheat/barley and cattle domestication ~7000 BCE), ground and polished stone axes/celts, handmade pottery, and pit dwellings (Burzahom, Kashmir); followed by the South Indian Megalithic Culture (iron age monuments, dolmens, cists, urn burials, Black and Red Ware).

coreConcepts.title: Palaeolithic Sequence in India: Lower, Middle, and Upper
coreConcepts.explanation:
The Palaeolithic (Old Stone Age) spanned the geological Pleistocene epoch.
1. Lower Palaeolithic:
- Sohan Tradition: Discovered by H. de Terra and T.T. Paterson (1939) in the Sohan river valley (Potwar plateau). Dominated by unifacial choppers and bifacial chopping tools manufactured on rounded river pebbles.
- Acheulian Tradition: Characterized by pear-shaped bifacial handaxes and cleavers shaped by soft hammer percussion (block-on-block, cylinder hammer technique). Landmark sites: Attirampakkam (Tamil Nadu, dated to ~1.5 mya), Hunsgi valley (Karnataka), and Bhimbetka rock shelters (Madhya Pradesh).
2. Middle Palaeolithic (Nevasan Culture):
- Identified by H.D. Sankalia at Nevasa on the Pravara river (Maharashtra). Made on fine-grained siliceous rocks (chert, jasper, agate) rather than quartzite. Tool types: side scrapers, end scrapers, points, and borers crafted using Levallois prepared-core technique.
3. Upper Palaeolithic:
- Characterized by specialized blade and burin industries produced through indirect percussion (punch technique). Major sites: Belan valley (UP), Patne (Maharashtra, ostrich eggshell beads), Kurnool caves (Andhra Pradesh, bone tools), and Renigunta.
keyTakeaways: Lower Palaeolithic: Sohan pebble tools (North) vs Acheulian Madrasian handaxes (South/Central).
Attirampakkam: Oldest Acheulian site in India (~1.5 million years old).
Middle Palaeolithic: 'Nevasan' flake industry based on fine cryptocrystalline silica (Sankalia).
Upper Palaeolithic: Blade and burin tools; Patne ostrich eggshell beads; Kurnool bone implements.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: CBSE/State Board Anthropology Class XII, Archaeological Anthropology, pp. 54-72.

coreConcepts.title: The Mesolithic Cultural Transition and Prehistoric Rock Art
coreConcepts.explanation:
With the onset of the warm, humid Holocene epoch (~10,000 BCE), megafauna retreated and lush flora expanded.
1. Microlithic Technology: Characterized by tiny stone tools (1-5 cm) struck from micro-blade cores. Includes non-geometric forms (scrapers, points) evolving into geometric microliths (crescents/lunates, triangles, trapezes) that were hafted onto bone or wooden shafts with natural resin to create composite hunting arrows, spears, and sickles.
2. Key Indian Mesolithic Settlements:
- Bagor (Rajasthan on Kothari river): Excavated by V.N. Misra; largest Mesolithic site in India showing early sheep/goat pastoralism.
- Langhnaj (Gujarat): Yielded 14 human burials and animal remains.
- Sarai Nahar Rai, Mahadaha, Damdama (Ganga valley, UP): Extended human burials with microlith grave goods and bone ornaments.
3. Prehistoric Rock Art at Bhimbetka:
- Discovered by V.S. Wakankar (1957) in Raisen district, MP (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Over 500 painted shelters portraying Mesolithic life: dynamic animal herds (bison, tiger, boar, deer), communal hunting scenes, stick-figure human dancers, and ritual processions painted using mineral pigments (red hematite, green copper minerals, white limestone).
keyTakeaways: Mesolithic hallmark: Geometric microliths (lunates, trapezes) used as composite tools.
Bagor: Largest Mesolithic campsite in India showing pastoral beginnings (V.N. Misra).
Bhimbetka: Discovered by V.S. Wakankar (1957); Mesolithic rock art depicting hunting and dancing in red and green.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Archaeological Anthropology Class XII, Section 2.3, pp. 74-84.

coreConcepts.title: The Neolithic Revolution and Megalithic Cultures of India
coreConcepts.explanation:
1. The Neolithic Revolution (V. Gordon Childe): Marked the decisive shift from food gathering to food production.
- Key Innovations: Ground and polished stone celts/axes with sharp working edges, plant domestication, animal husbandry, pottery manufacture (handmade progressing to slow-wheel), and sedentary village life.
- Regional Manifestations:
  • North-Western: Mehrgarh (Baluchistan, 7000 BCE): Earliest evidence of settled farming (barley, wheat, cattle/sheep rearing, mud-brick houses).
  • Northern (Kashmir Valley): Burzahom and Gufkral: Underground pit dwellings (protection against severe winter), polished celts, bone harpoons/needles, and unique dog burials alongside human masters.
  • Eastern & North-Eastern: Chirand (Bihar, famous for diverse bone implements), Daojali Hading and Sarutaru (Assam/Meghalaya, shouldered stone celts, cord-marked pottery).
  • Southern: Sanganakallu, Piklihal, Brahmagiri, Utnur: Characterized by ash mounds (burnt cattle-dung accumulations).
2. Megalithic Culture of South India:
- Iron Age culture (~1000 BCE - 100 CE) distinguished by monumental stone commemorative/burial structures.
- Monument Types: Dolmens (stone slab tables), Cists (underground stone boxes), Menhirs (monolithic upright standing stones), Cairn circles, Rock-cut caves, and Urn burials (Adichanallur, Tamil Nadu).
- Associated Artifacts: Black and Red Ware (BRW) pottery, iron weapons (swords, daggers, spears), and horse bits/trappings.
keyTakeaways: Neolithic hallmark: Ground/polished stone axes, food production, pottery, sedentary villages.
Mehrgarh: Earliest agricultural village in the subcontinent (~7000 BCE).
Burzahom: Pit dwellings, bone tools, dog-human burials.
Megaliths: Iron Age South Indian burials (Menhirs, Dolmens, Cists) with Black & Red Ware and iron weapons.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Archaeological Anthropology Class XII, Section 2.4 & 2.5, pp. 86-97.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Oldest Lower Palaeolithic Acheulian site in India (~1.5 million years old)
keyFacts.explanation: Located in the Kortallayar basin near Chennai, Tamil Nadu; excavated by Robert Bruce Foote (1863) and Shanti Pappu.
keyFacts.examTip: Robert Bruce Foote is honored as the 'Father of Indian Prehistory'.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Discovered: 1957 by V.S. Wakankar | Raisen, MP | UNESCO World Heritage Site
keyFacts.explanation: Continuous sequence from Lower Palaeolithic through Mesolithic; famous for vivid red and white rock art.
keyFacts.examTip: CUET asks who discovered Bhimbetka and what period the paintings predominantly belong to (Mesolithic).

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Neolithic culture of Kashmir Valley | Deep subterranean circular/oval pits
keyFacts.explanation: Inhabitants dug pit houses into karewa soil with post-holes for timber roofs to endure harsh Himalayan winters.
keyFacts.examTip: Also notable for unique burial of pet dogs along with human skeletons.

keyFacts.formulaOrFact: Signature pottery of the Indian Megalithic and Chalcolithic periods
keyFacts.explanation: Produced by inverted firing where interior and rim turn black while the exterior body turns oxidized red.
keyFacts.examTip: Universally found in South Indian iron-age megalithic graves.

workedExamples.question: Which legendary archaeologist is universally celebrated as the 'Father of Indian Prehistory' after discovering the first Acheulian palaeolithic handaxe at Pallavaram near Madras in 1863?
solutionSteps: Step 1: Recall the milestone event in Indian prehistory: In May 1863, a British geologist discovered a chipped stone handaxe in a gravel pit at Pallavaram, Tamil Nadu.
Step 2: That scientist was Robert Bruce Foote of the Geological Survey of India.
Step 3: This discovery initiated prehistoric research in the subcontinent, earning him the title 'Father of Indian Prehistory'.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: Robert Bruce Foote, Pallavaram, and 1863 form one of the most frequently asked historical trivia stems in Indian archaeology.

workedExamples.question: The Neolithic site of Burzahom situated in the Kashmir Valley is uniquely renowned for which distinctive architectural and cultural feature?

options.text: Subterranean pit dwellings dug into Karewa soil and burials of pet dogs with their masters

solutionSteps: Step 1: Identify the site: Burzahom (meaning 'place of birch trees'), located near Srinagar, Kashmir.
Step 2: Distinctive traits: Subterranean circular/oval pit houses designed to withstand freezing winter conditions, polished stone celts, bone harpoons, and pet dog skeletons buried with humans.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: Burzahom pit dwellings and dog burials are iconic NCERT archaeology facts.

howCuetAsks.typicalStem: Match Robert Bruce Foote, V.S. Wakankar, and H.D. Sankalia with Pallavaram handaxe, Bhimbetka rock art, and Nevasan culture.
howCuetAsks.strategy: Memorize: Foote = Pallavaram handaxe; Wakankar = Bhimbetka; Sankalia = Nevasa.

howCuetAsks.patternType: Stone Age Period to Tool Typology
howCuetAsks.typicalStem: Geometric microliths like trapezes, triangles, and lunates belong to which cultural period?

commonTraps.trap: Confusing Megalithic culture with Neolithic culture.
commonTraps.whyItTraps: Both involve large stone use, but Megalithic monuments belong to the Iron Age (~1000 BCE) featuring iron weapons and Black & Red Ware, whereas Neolithic cultures are stone-using farming communities with polished stone axes and no iron.
commonTraps.howToAvoid: Neolithic = Polished Stone / Farming; Megalithic = Giant stone burials / Iron Age.

commonTraps.trap: Believing Bhimbetka rock paintings are exclusively Upper Palaeolithic.
commonTraps.whyItTraps: While Upper Palaeolithic green figures exist, the vast majority of dynamic group hunting and dancing scenes belong to the Mesolithic period.
commonTraps.howToAvoid: Bhimbetka's peak artistic flowering is Mesolithic.

mnemonics.meaning: Palaeolithic = Pebble/Handaxe; Mesolithic = Microlith; Neolithic = Polished Celt; Megalith = Iron monument.

practiceQuestions.question: Who discovered the world-famous prehistoric rock art shelters of Bhimbetka in Madhya Pradesh in 1957?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Dr. V.S. Wakankar discovered the Bhimbetka rock shelters in 1957 while traveling by train through Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh.

practiceQuestions.question: The earliest verified evidence of settled agriculture (wheat and barley cultivation) and cattle pastoralism in the Indian subcontinent dating to circa 7000 BCE was excavated at:
practiceQuestions.explanation: Mehrgarh located on the Bolan River in Baluchistan (excavated by Jarrige) provides a continuous transition from aceramic neolithic farming (7000 BCE) to early chalcolithic life.

practiceQuestions.question: A single, massive upright standing monolithic stone erected as a memorial or funerary monument in Megalithic traditions is called a:
practiceQuestions.explanation: A Menhir (from Breton 'men' stone, 'hir' long) is a single, tall, unhewn or roughly dressed monolithic standing stone erected over or near burial spots.

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): The Mesolithic period in India witnessed a widespread adoption of tiny, geometric stone tools termed microliths.
Reason (R): Microliths were designed to be hafted as composite elements into wooden or bone handles to serve as sharp projectile arrowheads, harpoon barbs, and sickles suited for hunting smaller game.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Both statements are completely true and (R) explains the technological advantage of composite microlithic weaponry adapted to post-glacial Holocene environmental fauna.

practiceQuestions.question:
Match List-I (Archaeological Site) with List-II (Key Archaeological Feature):
List-I:
(P) Attirampakkam
(Q) Bhimbetka
(R) Burzahom
(S) Bagor

List-II:
(1) Subterranean Neolithic pit dwellings & dog burials
(2) Earliest Acheulian handaxes (~1.5 mya)
(3) Largest Indian Mesolithic campsite with sheep/goat pastoralism
(4) Mesolithic rock paintings depicting hunting scenes
practiceQuestions.explanation: Attirampakkam = Acheulian handaxes; Bhimbetka = Mesolithic rock paintings; Burzahom = Pit dwellings & dog burials; Bagor = Mesolithic campsite with pastoralism.

practiceQuestions.question: Which distinctive pottery type characterized by an inverted firing technique resulting in a black interior and red exterior is universally found in South Indian Megalithic burials?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Black and Red Ware (BRW) is the quintessential ceramic industry associated with South Indian Megalithic burial cists and urns.

practiceQuestions.question: The Middle Palaeolithic industry of India, designated as the 'Nevasan Culture' by H.D. Sankalia, was characterized by tools made primarily of:

options.text: Fine cryptocrystalline siliceous stones like chert, jasper, and chalcedony

practiceQuestions.explanation: The Nevasan Middle Palaeolithic shifted away from quartzite cobbles toward fine-grained silica minerals (chert, jasper, agate) to manufacture refined scrapers, borers, and points.

practiceQuestions.question: The prominent archaeological site of Chirand in the Saran district of Bihar is widely renowned in Indian Neolithic studies for yielding an extraordinary wealth of:

options.text: Diverse bone and antler implements (harpoons, needles, scrapers)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Chirand is celebrated for its dense bone tool technology made from deer antlers, including scrapers, chisels, needles, and harpoons during the Neolithic period.

practiceQuestions.question: The Southern Neolithic culture (e.g., Utnur, Piklihal, Kudatini) is famously marked by the presence of 'Ash Mounds', which originated from:

options.text: Accumulated, ritualistically burnt heaps of cattle dung in pastoral stockades
Cremation of entire villages after plagues

practiceQuestions.explanation: Excavations by Raymond Allchin proved that Neolithic ash mounds represent repeated, seasonal burning of accumulated cow dung within circular pastoral penning enclosures.

practiceQuestions.question: Engraved fragments of ostrich eggshell beads dating to the Upper Palaeolithic period were excavated in notable abundance at which Indian site?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Patne in Jalgaon district, Maharashtra (excavated by S.A. Sali) yielded engraved ostrich eggshell fragments and finished disc beads dating to the Upper Palaeolithic (~25,000 BCE).

prerequisites: Human Evolution, Primatology, Genetics, Human Variation

diagram.title: Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, Neolithic and Megalithic Cultures of India
diagram.caption: Anthropology schematic and conceptual diagram for Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, Neolithic and Megalithic Cultures of India
diagram.code:
<svg viewBox="0 0 800 480" width="100%" height="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <rect width="800" height="480" fill="#fdfbf7" rx="12"/>
  <text x="400" y="32" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="20" font-weight="bold" fill="#78350f">Prehistoric Lithic Sequence & Cultural Epochs of India</text>
  
  <!-- 4-Stage Horizontal Progression -->
  <g transform="translate(45, 60)">
    <!-- Stage 1: Palaeolithic -->
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="165" height="150" rx="8" fill="#fff7ed" stroke="#ea580c" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="82" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#9a3412">1. Palaeolithic</text>
    <text x="82" y="42" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#c2410c">Pleistocene Epoch</text>
    <text x="10" y="66" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#7c2d12">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Lower:</tspan> Sohan pebbles &</text>
    <text x="10" y="80" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#7c2d12">  Acheulian handaxes</text>
    <text x="10" y="98" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#7c2d12">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Middle:</tspan> Nevasan flakes</text>
    <text x="10" y="112" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#7c2d12">  (scrapers, borers)</text>
    <text x="10" y="130" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#7c2d12">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Upper:</tspan> Blades & burins</text>
    <text x="10" y="142" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#9a3412">Attirampakkam, Kurnool</text>

    <!-- Arrow 1 -->
    <line x1="165" y1="75" x2="185" y2="75" stroke="#ea580c" stroke-width="2"/>

    <!-- Stage 2: Mesolithic -->
    <rect x="185" y="0" width="165" height="150" rx="8" fill="#fefce8" stroke="#ca8a04" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="267" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#854d0e">2. Mesolithic</text>
    <text x="267" y="42" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#a16207">Early Holocene</text>
    <text x="195" y="66" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#713f12">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Microliths:</tspan> 1–5 cm</text>
    <text x="195" y="80" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#713f12">  Geometric trapezes,</text>
    <text x="195" y="94" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#713f12">  triangles, lunates</text>
    <text x="195" y="112" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#713f12">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Bhimbetka Art:</tspan> Hunting,</text>
    <text x="195" y="126" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#713f12">  dancing in red hematite</text>
    <text x="195" y="142" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#854d0e">Bagor, Langhnaj, Sarai Nahar</text>

    <!-- Arrow 2 -->
    <line x1="350" y1="75" x2="370" y2="75" stroke="#ca8a04" stroke-width="2"/>

    <!-- Stage 3: Neolithic -->
    <rect x="370" y="0" width="165" height="150" rx="8" fill="#f0fdf4" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="452" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#15803d">3. Neolithic</text>
    <text x="452" y="42" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#166534">Food Production</text>
    <text x="380" y="66" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#14532d">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Polished stone celts</tspan></text>
    <text x="380" y="80" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#14532d">• Plant & cattle farming</text>
    <text x="380" y="96" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#14532d">• Handmade/Wheel pottery</text>
    <text x="380" y="114" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#14532d">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Burzahom:</tspan> Pit dwellings</text>
    <text x="380" y="128" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#14532d">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Mehrgarh:</tspan> 7000 BCE</text>
    <text x="380" y="142" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#15803d">Chirand, Daojali Hading</text>

    <!-- Arrow 3 -->
    <line x1="535" y1="75" x2="555" y2="75" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="2"/>

    <!-- Stage 4: Megalithic -->
    <rect x="555" y="0" width="160" height="150" rx="8" fill="#f8fafc" stroke="#475569" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="635" y="24" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e293b">4. Megalithic</text>
    <text x="635" y="42" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#475569">Iron Age Commemoration</text>
    <text x="565" y="66" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#334155">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Monuments:</tspan> Dolmens,</text>
    <text x="565" y="80" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#334155">  cists, menhirs, cairns</text>
    <text x="565" y="98" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#334155">• <tspan font-weight="bold">Pottery:</tspan> Black & Red</text>
    <text x="565" y="112" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#334155">  Ware (BRW)</text>
    <text x="565" y="128" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#334155">• Iron weapons & horse bits</text>
    <text x="565" y="142" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10" fill="#1e293b">Adichanallur, Brahmagiri</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Landmark Sites & Technology Deep Dive -->
  <rect x="45" y="235" width="345" height="215" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#fed7aa" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <text x="217" y="262" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#9a3412">Key Prehistoric Sites & Pioneers</text>

  <rect x="60" y="278" width="315" height="48" rx="6" fill="#fff7ed"/>
  <text x="70" y="296" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#7c2d12">Robert Bruce Foote (1863):</text>
  <text x="70" y="312" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#9a3412">• First handaxe at Pallavaram; Father of Indian Prehistory</text>

  <rect x="60" y="332" width="315" height="52" rx="6" fill="#fff7ed"/>
  <text x="70" y="350" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#7c2d12">V.S. Wakankar (1957) - Bhimbetka:</text>
  <text x="70" y="366" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#9a3412">• 500+ painted rock shelters; UNESCO World Heritage</text>

  <rect x="60" y="390" width="315" height="48" rx="6" fill="#fff7ed"/>
  <text x="70" y="408" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#7c2d12">H.D. Sankalia - Nevasa:</text>
  <text x="70" y="424" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#9a3412">• Established Middle Palaeolithic 'Nevasan' flake industry</text>

  <!-- Megalithic Monument Typology -->
  <rect x="410" y="235" width="345" height="215" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <text x="582" y="262" text-anchor="middle" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e293b">Megalithic Monuments of South India</text>

  <rect x="425" y="278" width="315" height="48" rx="6" fill="#f8fafc"/>
  <text x="435" y="296" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#334155">Menhir:</text>
  <text x="435" y="312" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#475569">• Single upright monolithic standing commemorative stone</text>

  <rect x="425" y="332" width="315" height="48" rx="6" fill="#f8fafc"/>
  <text x="435" y="350" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#334155">Dolmen & Cist:</text>
  <text x="435" y="366" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#475569">• Dolmen: Above-ground table stone | Cist: Box-like grave box</text>

  <rect x="425" y="386" width="315" height="52" rx="6" fill="#f8fafc"/>
  <text x="435" y="404" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#334155">Urn Burial & Cairn Circles:</text>
  <text x="435" y="420" font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" font-size="10.5" fill="#475569">• Earthenware jars with bones (Adichanallur) surrounded by boulders</text>
</svg>

pyqExample.question: Match Robert Bruce Foote, V.S. Wakankar, and H.D. Sankalia with Pallavaram handaxe, Bhimbetka rock art, and Nevasan culture.
pyqExample.explanation: Memorize: Foote = Pallavaram handaxe; Wakankar = Bhimbetka; Sankalia = Nevasa.
